record.paper_title: On some open problems in Diophantine approximation
record.original_question: For a real number x, let ||x|| denote the distance from x to the nearest integer. For each integer n >= 2 and every n-tuple of real numbers theta_1, ..., theta_n, must lim inf as q tends to infinity of q ||q theta_1|| ... ||q theta_n|| equal 0?

evidence.quote: here and in the sequel || · || stands for the distance to the nearest integer
The similar multidimensional problem is for given n ⩾ 2 to prove that for any reals θ1 , ..., θn one has lim inf q ||qθ1 || · · · ||qθn || = 0.
This problem is not solved for any n ⩾ 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a real number $x$, let $\|x\|$ denote the distance from $x$ to the nearest integer. Fix an integer $n \geq 2$. Prove or disprove: for every $n$-tuple of real numbers $\theta_1, \theta_2, \ldots, \theta_n$, one has
$$\liminf_{q \to \infty,\ q \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}} q\,\|q\theta_1\|\,\|q\theta_2\|\cdots\|q\theta_n\| = 0.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The case n=2 is the classical Littlewood conjecture, which remains open. The strongest partial result is due to Einsiedler, Katok, and Lindenstrauss (2006), showing that the set of counterexamples has Hausdorff dimension zero. The multidimensional generalization for n ≥ 2 is also unresolved as of 2025–2026, with ongoing work on variants and restricted classes.

status_evidence.title: Littlewood conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The Littlewood conjecture remains open; the strongest known result is that the set of exceptions has Hausdorff dimension zero (Einsiedler, Katok, Lindenstrauss).
status_evidence.claim: The Littlewood conjecture (n=2) is still open.

status_evidence.title: The Littlewood conjecture for a restricted class of pairs
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work proves the Littlewood conjecture for restricted classes of badly approximable pairs.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues on partial cases, indicating the conjecture is still open.

status_evidence.title: Variants of the Littlewood conjecture (2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent 2025 article discussing variants of the Littlewood conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: As of 2025 the conjecture and its multidimensional analogues remain a subject of active research.
